title: Buddy Petit's trumpet style and playing
summary: Howard describes Petit as an open-horn player, sweet but good, with fine fingering and tongue, who played the Red Book numbers at dances and parties.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: What style did he play? I mean can you describe it? I mean I know you can't go into great detail without actually playing the part and trumpet. I mean did he use much mute work like Chris Kelly or was it mostly open?
No, no it was open.
Just about all of them.
But now he was no high note man but. He might turn this to him. Huh?
Let's close this a little bit too. He was no high note man.
He wasn't high note though? No but he was a trumpet player.
Was he a sort of rough or sweet style or what?

Sweet but good. Good. See when I met him, first time I met him it was in Bugalusa. Yeah. Bugalusa. And he was playing a lot of horn then. After that he came back home here and played a trumpet. No way he wasn't too much with that mute. I mean he didn't use that, he played, but he could fingers so good. Yeah.
Did he play very loud or soft mostly or what was it? Very?
No he could go loud and get soft in any way. He had a fine tongue, something like bunk. Yeah.
See?
But he could finger that thing. And he played everything in the Red Book. We called it Red Book all the numbers that he played all of that.
Yeah. Did he read much or used music never? Well I don't know, I wouldn't know about his reading ability. Naturally he wouldn't have the music much on the job I guess.
No I don't know if they'd have somebody that worked with him, you see, to know that. But I would have played, but I would have played, you know, there ain't no music or nothing like that.
When he played around here was it mostly big dances like at the economy? Sam played in all those places.
Fabio and all those places he played all of that.
Ever played in little dunks like in Connery Bar Rooms and things too? All that goes, sure.
Just everything.
It's like Chris.
Chris played a lot of parties, we used to have parties. People say there are parties on Monday nights at different places. At the house, the house party. Well they have four or five pieces.
